sequence.description: Brokered-flow attack: attempt token exchange with a subject_token that is not bound to the configured OIDC connector trust anchor (issuer/JWKS).
sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex token exchange must verify the submitted subject_token against the configured connector trust anchor; a token minted under a different issuer/JWKS must not be consumed as if verified for this connector.

Dex accepted a subject_token with nbf far in the future during token exchange; not-yet-valid token was treated as fresh.

finding.sequence_description: Attempt to escalate scopes/claims during RFC8693 token exchange by using an ID token obtained with minimal scopes, then requesting expanded scopes in the exchange.
finding.description: [LLM-Judge] Token exchange succeeded and produced a session with expanded attributes (groups/policies/display_name) even though the initial minimal-scope authorization code grant failed and no ID token/session token was obtained.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Token exchange succeeded and produced a session with expanded attributes (groups/policies/display_name) even though the initial minimal-scope authorization code grant failed and no ID token/session token was obtained.

sequence.description: Attempt to escalate scopes/claims during RFC8693 token exchange by using an ID token obtained with minimal scopes, then requesting expanded scopes in the exchange.
sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I5: Exchanged token must not include claims/permissions beyond the upstream intent (originally granted scopes) and broker policy; expanded scopes in token exchange should be rejected or not reflected in resulting identity claims.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token exchange accepted expanded scopes and returned group claims even though original upstream intent only requested 'openid email' (scope escalation via exchange).

finding.sequence_description: Probe whether Dex mints tokens for a different audience (client) via RFC8693 token exchange without explicit trustedPeers authorization (cross-client trust bypass). Uses two identities to ensure the system is responsive and to detect unintended permission/identity changes.
finding.description: [LLM-Judge] RFC8693 token exchange succeeded (HTTP 200) even though the normal authorization-code token exchange failed, suggesting token exchange may be usable without a valid prior OIDC grant/session (potential cross-client/trust bypass depending on requested audience/subject_token validation).

evidence.llm_judge_description: RFC8693 token exchange succeeded (HTTP 200) even though the normal authorization-code token exchange failed, suggesting token exchange may be usable without a valid prior OIDC grant/session (potential cross-client/trust bypass depending on requested audience/subject_token validation).

sequence.description: Probe whether Dex mints tokens for a different audience (client) via RFC8693 token exchange without explicit trustedPeers authorization (cross-client trust bypass). Uses two identities to ensure the system is responsive and to detect unintended permission/identity changes.
sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I5: Token exchange must not allow a client to obtain tokens for an unauthorized audience (different client) unless broker policy explicitly allows it (e.g., trustedPeers). Effective permissions/claims must remain within UpstreamIntent ∩ BrokerPolicy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted token exchange for an unauthorized audience (cross-client token minting) without explicit trustedPeers/broker policy authorization, violating authorization binding.
